## 7 · Where the spec lives, and the artifacts around it

### 7.1 · The spec lives in the example, not in the docs tree

**A product spec belongs at `examples/cp-NN-<slug>/spec/CP-SPEC-NNN_<Name>.md`,
and is created there at Gate 1.** It is never authored in
`public/reference/specifications/`.

This follows from §2 rather than from filing preference. A spec whose §D steps
are discharged by witnesses in `artifacts/assembly-recipe.yaml`, and whose
emitted contract is validated by CI against code in the same directory, has to
be **versioned with the thing that proves it**. Move it into a documentation
tree and the claims and their evidence can drift in separate commits — which is
the entire failure this recipe exists to prevent.

The two trees have different jobs:

| Path | Holds | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `examples/cp-NN-<slug>/spec/` | **product specifications** — one per example, co-versioned with the code that discharges them | `CP-SPEC-000-institutional-holders.md` |
| `public/reference/specifications/` | **reference documents** — things that govern specs but describe no product | `Context_Product_Specification_Standard_v0-3.md`, this recipe |

**ONE CANONICAL SPEC, AND NO SECOND COPY THAT CAN DRIFT.** A product
specification lives in its example's `spec/` directory and **is not duplicated
into `public/`**. There is no second location and no per-spec nav entry.

| | Where |
|---|---|
| **Canonical, and the only copy** | `examples/cp-NN-<slug>/spec/`, from Gate 1 onward — versioned with the artifacts and code that discharge it |
| **`public/reference/specifications/`** | reference documents that **govern** specs and describe no product: the authoring standard, this recipe, the delivery companion |

Public documentation **may reference or summarize** a CP-SPEC — link to it,
quote a clause, explain what a rung proves. It must not create a second copy of
the document.

**This corrects what this section used to say, and the correction is a
documentation-rule fix rather than any product's deviation** (Dave,
2026-09-12). The previous text directed a copy into
`public/reference/specifications/` with a nav entry after Gate 2, and cited
`mkdocs.yml` for it. `mkdocs.yml` says the opposite, in a ruling of the same
author dated 2026-08-29:

> *"Individual CP-SPECs do NOT live here. A specification lives in its own
> example's `spec/` directory, beside the artifacts and code it governs.
> `CP-SPEC-001` sat here only to bootstrap the authoring process and was deleted
> at `59831ea5` once it had served that purpose — by then it had drifted to 640
> lines against a 1,355-line canonical source, silently dropping every section
> that recorded an open question."*

**The precedent is unanimous and was measured before this edit: no CP-SPEC for
`cp-00` through `cp-08` is published under `public/` at all.** Eight gates
closed without it. The surviving instruction here was stale, and it was caught
at rung 9's Gate 2 by an executor who stopped rather than following it.

**Why the deleted copy is the argument.** A specification is proven by the
artifacts and tests beside it; a copy somewhere else is proven by nothing, and
the first thing it loses is the sections recording open questions — which is
exactly what happened, and it happened silently, because a stale copy renders
perfectly well.

> ⚠️ `public/` has a strict docs build. **Any file you add under `public/`
> without a nav entry fails `mkdocs build --strict`.** That still holds for the
> reference documents this directory does carry.

> **`CP-SPEC-001_Counterparty_Reference_Snapshot.md` is a deliberately placed
> exemplar — *"what a spec would look like for counterparty reference"* (Dave,
> 2026-08-29) — and it is a **control, not a source.**
>
> The plan for rung 01 is that you author the spec **fresh from this recipe**,
> and Dave then compares your output against that file **by hand**. That
> comparison is a test of the recipe as much as of your spec, and it only works
> if you have not read CP-SPEC-001 as an input. **Deltas are expected and are
> the point.** Where your spec differs, the difference is the finding.
>
> So: author at `examples/cp-01-counterparty-reference-snapshot/spec/`. Do not
> copy from CP-SPEC-001, do not reconcile against it, and do not treat its
> values as authoritative — it predates the example-based structure, has no
> `artifacts/`, no witnesses, and the error classes cataloged in §10.2.

### 7.2 · The example layout

The spec is one file in a runnable example. Match `cp-01`'s layout:

```
examples/cp-NN-<slug>/
├── spec/CP-SPEC-NNN_<Product_Name>.md
├── artifacts/
│   ├── assembly-recipe.yaml   ← §D.2 as data, with a WITNESS per step
│   ├── expected.yaml          ← what the served product should contain
│   ├── question.yaml          ← the caller's vocabulary, read-side
│   └── ttl.yaml               ← the class TTL and its ceiling
├── assembler.py  produce.py  run.py  deployment.py
├── backends.yaml  ccf_config.yaml
├── page/                      ← build_page.py + template.html committed, render is not
├── README.md
└── summary_explanations.md    ← the banker-facing document
```

**The `page/` directory and `summary_explanations.md` are not optional**, and
what goes in them, plus the `example-cp-NN` target, the venv discipline and
the validation pass, are governed by
[How an example is delivered](example_delivery.md) — which is authoritative for
everything downstream of this section. This diagram is the summary; that
document is the recipe.

All `artifacts/*.yaml` validate against
`docs/schemas/ccf.declared-artifact.json`.

Follow `cp-00`'s `expected.yaml` discipline: **it derives nothing from a run.**
When artifacts change, run the suite, review the failure, and deliberately edit
the file in the same commit — so an expected-output change is an edit to a
reviewed artifact rather than a refreshed transcript.

---

## 8 · Definition of done — the specification

Ship when all of these hold. This is the standard's §15, plus what this pipeline
adds.

**These are the SPECIFICATION's conditions and they are half the deliverable.**
The example's conditions — the `make` target, the venv, the README run block,
the documentation page, the banker summary, the verbatim-output check and the
validation pass — are [How an example is delivered](example_delivery.md) §11.
Both lists must hold before anything is presented to Dave.

- **The spec was approved by Dave at Gate 1 before any implementation code was
  written**, and every Gate-2 deviation from the approved design was taken back
  to him rather than absorbed
- All seven sections present in order, with §0, front matter, capability gate
  and the data banner
- Four-question result carried from the vault **including partials**
- Nine contract elements populated, Assembly Mode with rationale
- Classification, residency, information-barrier complete; model-risk complete
  for Modes 2/3 or "not applicable" for Mode 1
- Every §C element has SOR, provenance class, classification, capability class,
  G dimension and ontology IRI — and **no §C row names a database**
- Capability decomposition present where the estate answer is unknown, with
  interim posture
- Correlation key stated with **measured** coverage, or the measurement named as
  an F.2 gap
- Every §D step names one closed-vocabulary operator with capability class,
  emits, failure behavior and budget — **and has a witness in
  `assembly-recipe.yaml`**
- The four composition invariants hold: Policy before any graph read · Resolve
  before Traversal · Enrich always batched · algorithmic substrate before any
  semantic stage
- Determinism class stated with an enum value; payload hash defined
- Replay statement plus a numbered falsifiable replay test that has been **run
  and observed to fail** when the snapshot is bypassed
- Emitted contract shown with types, conformant to the §8 envelope, passing
  `extra=forbid` in CI; error taxonomy mapped to steps
- Six universal gates plus product-specific gates with fixture IDs, **each made
  to fail deliberately at least once**
- Half-life table carries calibration basis and owner per row, and **no λ_c is a
  publication cadence**
- Per-component debt table present; contributions checked against
  `debt_tolerance`
- Materialization posture derived from measured λ_c against read frequency;
  cache key complete
- Every `no` or `partial` in §F has a named gap owner; volumetrics stated
- §G complete; consumers named individually; cascading supersession targets named
- **F.2 register complete — every `[TBC]` carries an owning agent**
- Acceptance criteria are failable assertions; blocking decisions named

---

## 9 · Cross-agent placeholder discipline

| Situation | Write |
|---|---|
| Vault has not framed something you need | `[TBC — vault]` + what you asked |
| Data reality unknown or unmeasured | `[TBC — ccf_dataprep]` + the measurement needed |
| Vault framing and build evidence conflict | `[TBC — ruling]` + both readings, verbatim |
| You have not built it yet | `[TBC — this build, phase Pn]` |

Never `[TBC]` bare. An unowned marker is an unassigned risk, and the F.2
register is what makes it collectable.

---

## 10 · Known conflicts — do not resolve these silently

**10.1 · `counterparty-reference-snapshot` grade and coverage — NOT blocking.
Author to the vault.**

The vault's scope boundary says *"identity only — no exposure, **no grade**, no
relationship."* CP-SPEC-001's payload declares `internal_risk_grade`,
`coverage_rm_id`, `coverage_team`, `coverage_lob` and an `internal_risk_grade`
freshness class. `ccf_dataprep` built to the vault's reading and carries **none**
of those fields.

**This is not a conflict between two authorities.** Scope boundary is the
**vault's term** under §1, and CP-SPEC-001 is an exemplar for later comparison
(§7.1), not a source. So:

- **Author to the vault's scope.** No internal overlay in rung 01.
- The overlay is then **not a debt component at all**, so CP-SPEC-001's
  0.30-against-0.25 `debt_tolerance` collision — and the `409` it implies —
  **does not arise.** That failure exists only under a per-component table
  counting a field the spec does not carry.
- **`ccf_dataprep` is already aligned.** Nothing needs regenerating.

If your build disproves the vault's scope, that is a §11 return, not a reason to
stop.

> **A ruling that was inferred rather than made.** On 2026-08-29 Dave pasted
> **both** documents — the vault's `counterparty-reference-snapshot` article at
> 03:23 MST with *"this is the one we need to build to"*, and the authoring
> Standard nine minutes later. Together that is the framing input and the
> structural basis: **the direction was unambiguous.**
>
> What it was not is a decision on the grade/coverage conflict, which §10.1 had
> marked blocking. **A document handover settles what you build to; it does not
> close a named conflict.** Those are closed by an explicit decision, named, or
> not at all — so **ask for one by name and wait.** Declining to close it alone
> was correct, and the inference pointed the right way.

**10.2 · Vault articles carry theoretical values that have been measurably
wrong.** Documented cases in `counterparty-reference-snapshot`: λ_c set to
publication cadence (24h vs ~365d); materialization posture inverted as a
consequence; `operators_invoked` as bare names; missing `payload_hash`,
`model_record` and the per-attribute authority field; a parameter surface
missing `debt_tolerance` and the inert `as_of`. **Assume the same class of error
in the other twenty.** Take framing from the vault; take values from your build.

**10.3 · The `references/` copies are history, not sources.**
`references/CP-SPEC-001_..._v2.md` and
`references/CP-SPEC-001_..._v0-3-restructure.md` are prior drafts. Read them for
audit history; author nothing from them. Same standing as CP-SPEC-001 itself
(§7.1).

**10.4 · Twenty vault articles are on the Q019 form** where §F means
*Manufacture envelope*. Resolve by heading name.

**10.5 · The vault's catalog count is stale** — it says 22 product specs in two
places; the measured figure is **21**, of which **20** declare no Assembly Mode.

---

## 11 · The return path

When your build contradicts an input, **send it back** — the failure this
pipeline exists to prevent is a correction that stalls at the boundary.

- **To the vault:** write into `~/.agent-exchange/<your-agent-id>/outbox/` as
  `<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ>-<slug>.tmp/` containing `message.md` plus attachments,
  **then rename to drop `.tmp`** — the rename is what publishes it. A message
  left as `.tmp` never arrives, and this has already happened once: dataprep's
  2026-08-28 consumer signal sat unpublished until it was found by hand. State
  what your document **removes**, not only what it adds.
- **To ccf_dataprep:** same channel, their box is `ccf-dataprep`.
- **Your box is `ccf-sdk`** — `/home/parkave/.agent-exchange/ccf-sdk/`, with
  `inbox/`, `outbox/` and `_archive/`. Use that id, not a new one: a duplicate
  under a different id splits you into two agents.

Send back at minimum: any scope-boundary conflict, any λ_c the build disproves,
any element the vault names that the estate cannot supply, and any capability
the estate fails.

---

## 12 · Summary

1. Read the vault article — take **framing**, never values.
2. Pull the data reality from `ccf_dataprep` — **measure**, never assume.
3. Structure to the **Standard v0.3**, templated on **CP-SPEC-000**.
4. **Author the spec first, at `examples/cp-NN-<slug>/spec/`** — it is step one
   of the example project, and it lives with the code that will prove it. Mark
   what only the build can know as `[TBC — this build]`.
5. **▶ Send it to Dave. Stop. Nothing is implemented until he approves it.**
6. Build the example; fill the measured terms; clear every `[TBC]`. A build that
   disproves an approved term is a **deviation** — take it back, do not absorb it.
7. Never write another agent's term. `[TBC — owner]` instead.
8. Every claim discharged by something that runs; every gate made to fail once.
9. Send contradictions back, and **remember the rename**.
10. Work the ladder in order. Complexity is the vault's call, not yours.

# CP-08 — Covenant-in-Force As-Of

> **Current run instructions — 18 October 2026:** checked against [SDK `v1.0.2@5f85b389`](https://github.com/drcastillo/ccf_code/blob/5f85b389efe9e4b1de62e84a5af62ca4b2e12178/examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/README.md). Use [the shared setup and configuration rules](../../../examples/CONFIGURATION.md), Fluree **4.2.4** where required, explicit ports and complete connection strings. The qualified source/specification pins below preserve earlier evidence; they do not select the checkout used by these commands.

**Business-to-spec companion:** [Analysis](CP08_COVENANT_IN_FORCE_AS_OF_ANALYSIS.md) · [HTML reading edition](CP08_COVENANT_IN_FORCE_AS_OF_ANALYSIS.html).

**Qualified SDK:** `drcastillo/ccf_code/main@a4cf2fb74af4964dcfee29d210d17d94b909d78d`  
**README:** `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/README.md`  
**Qualified specification:** `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/spec/CP-SPEC-008_Covenant_In_Force_As_Of.md`  
**Qualified source:** `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of`

> **Read the README and the qualified specification before opening the implementation code.**

## Start with the completed specification

For this shipped example, the design work is already complete. **Do not draft a new spec.**

Open the qualified SDK specification first:

`examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/spec/CP-SPEC-008_Covenant_In_Force_As_Of.md`

Read it before the Python:

| Spec section | What to learn | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| §A | decision, consumer, counterfactual, scope | README + acceptance tests |
| §B | contract, request, TTL, policy/perspective | `ccf_config.yaml` + payload |
| §C | sources, identity, ontology, data traps | acquisition + environment/source declarations |
| §D | operators, projection, gates | `acquisition.py`, `deployment.py`, `projection.py`, `produce.py` |
| §E | half-life, Context Debt, materialization | config + assessment code |
| §F | source readiness and limitations | environment/source artifacts + findings |
| §G | acceptance and operational evidence | tests, gates, run evidence |

As you read the code, ask: **which approved spec term is this implementing?**

## Why this example exists

Introduces two independent time axes: when something was true and when the bank knew/recorded it. The same facility and valid date can produce a different governed answer when known_as_of moves.

## The question

> Which covenant/amendment terms were in force at the business instant, and which of those were actually known to the institution at the knowledge instant?

## What to understand before you run it

- Valid time answers 'was it in force?'; assertion/knowledge time answers 'had we booked/known it?'.
- A current-state SELECT cannot reconstruct both axes.
- The example deliberately withdrew an unsupported supersession claim when the estate did not contain evidence for it.

## Prerequisites

Run from the `ccf_code` repository root.

```bash
make venv
```

Use the qualified/restored demonstration estate and read-only source credentials. This adoption guide uses placeholders even when the source README names a local development host.

```bash
export CCF_CP_08_FLUREE_URL='http://<fluree-host>:<port>'
export CCF_CP_08_FLUREE_LEDGER='fibo-v2'
export CCF_CP_08_POSTGRES_DSN='host=<host> port=<port> dbname=<database> user=<read-only-user> password=<password>'
export CCF_CP_08_POSTGRES_SCHEMA='ccf_v2'
```

## Files to read

| Path | Why |
|---|---|
| `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/spec/` | Two-axis temporal contract and the Gate-1 correction that removed unsupported supersession. |
| `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/artifacts/` | Question/temporal/gate evidence. |
| `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/acquisition.py / deployment.py` | Dual temporal filtering and source mapping. |
| `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/projection.py` | Admitted amendments/covenants. |
| `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/produce.py` | Governed product path. |
| `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/run.py` | Pinned forensic question. |
| `examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/README.md` | Measured story and limitations. |

## Run it

```bash
make venv
PYTHONPATH=src:runtime .venv/bin/python examples/cp-08-covenant-in-force-as-of/run.py
PYTHONPATH=.:src:runtime .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/examples/test_cp_08_output.py -q
```

An intentional governed refusal may produce a non-zero example process exit. Read the reported refusal before treating non-zero as a broken deployment.

## What you should observe

- At the pinned example, one amendment is both in force and known while a second is already in force but excluded because it was not yet booked at known_as_of.
- Moving known_as_of later admits the later-booked amendment without changing the business valid-time question.
- Current covenant terms are labeled as current/unversioned when the estate cannot prove historical supersession.

Exact content addresses, replay references, timestamps and measured figures should be checked against the qualified example's committed tests/transcripts rather than copied from memory.

## How the example works

```
source evidence
  ↓ acquisition
SignalEnvelope(s)
  ↓ governed assembly / L3
GraphView
  ↓ L4 operators
admitted/computed context
  ↓ Π
candidate product
  ↓ L6 gates + Debt fulfillment
served product OR governed refusal
```

This rung's distinctive behavior is described above; the listed source files show the implementation seam where it enters.

## Variations to try

| Purpose | Command | Expected semantic change |
|---|---|---|
| Knowledge instant equals valid instant | `set/request known_as_of=2025-09-09 for as_of=2025-09-09` | Only evidence booked by that date is admitted. |
| Later knowledge instant | `set/request known_as_of=2025-12-31 for as_of=2025-09-09` | Later-booked but already-effective amendment becomes admissible. |

## Validate it

```bash
PYTHONPATH=.:src:runtime .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/examples/test_cp_08_output.py -q
```

Do not stop at the happy path. The qualified SDK example's gate/sabotage tests are the evidence that the behavior is load-bearing.

## What this example proves

- Valid time and assertion/knowledge time are separate governed dimensions.
- Unsupported historical claims should be withdrawn rather than simulated.
- Temporal reconstruction can materially change the admitted evidence.

## What it does not prove

- Historical covenant supersession in this estate; the measured estate did not contain it.
- That every domain requires two time axes.

## Spec → code lesson for Cowork

Use CP-08 when the approved spec distinguishes what was true from what was known. Cowork must generate two separately testable filters and must not collapse them into one as_of.

Product-specific values, thresholds, source names and policy must come from the **new approved spec/evidence**, never from this demonstration by convenience.

CP-09 — Treasury Liquidity Position
Business-to-spec journey · Final specification · Included sources

CP-09 — Treasury Liquidity Position — Analysis

Audience: banking SME and Information Architect. Purpose: reconstruct the journey from the business problem to this example’s final specification.

Final specification: examples/cp-09-treasury-liquidity-position/spec/CP-SPEC-009_Treasury_Liquidity_Position.md, read directly from drcastillo/ccf_code at 37ac3055fd64ed64d78c6fd5555d79e451859153. Open the included final spec. Its recorded decisions, corrections, findings and placeholders are the destination of this walkthrough. The Standard v0.3 supplies the template and the generation recipe explains the ownership and evidence sequence.

The figures below are the final spec’s teaching-estate measurements or declared design values. They are not new runtime measurements. Once the design journey is understood, continue with the implementation walkthrough.

Start with the treasury decision and the age of each input

A treasury officer needs to understand a client's liquidity position under the mandate, concentration limits and regulatory posture applicable to the decision. The tempting answer is one total with one freshness label. The final spec rejects that shortcut: an intraday rate, a daily FX reference, a filing-period cash figure, an undated holding and a policy effective date do not measure the same kind of time.

The SME must also distinguish within limit, breach and limit unknown. At the measured anchor there are seven counterparties: one breach, three within limit and three with no evaluable limit. Coverage is 4/7, not seven reassuring verdicts. Across the estate, limits cover 60 of 103 holder/counterparty pairs. The second-largest anchor exposure has no limit and exceeds two limits that do exist. Treating missing policy as compliance would change the banking decision.

The resulting product serves a position and its qualifications. It does not optimize an allocation or generate proposals. These boundaries belong in the specification before an implementer decides what a helpful-looking output should contain.

Give each business input its contractual place — Standard §0–§B → final §0–§B

Element Value
Schema treasury_liquidity_position — entities cmns-org:LegalEntity, fibo-fbc-pas-caa:DepositAccount, fibo-fbc-pas-caa:InvestmentAccount, fibo-sec-dbt-bnd:TreasuryBill, fibo-sec-fun-fun:MutualFund, fibo-sec-dbt-tsd:CommercialPaper; measures fibo-ind-ir-ir:ReferenceInterestRate, fibo-ind-fx-fx:QuotedExchangeRate, fibo-fnd-acc-cur:MonetaryAmount; relationships ex:heldAt, ex:concentratedIn, ex:setOffAgainst; policy ex:RegulatoryPosture. Machine-readable at schemas/treasury_liquidity_position.v1.json
Freshness SLA Per signal class, and the classes do not share a clock — §B.6. Intraday rate 15 min · FX reference 1 day · filing-period cash 90 days · regulatory posture governed by effectivity, not by age · holdings unobserved and therefore unclaimable
TTL 15 minutes · ttl_anchor: from_decision. expires_at = decision_instant + 15m. A request pinned to a past as_of is a forensic reconstruction and does not decay; the payload says so rather than publishing a window that misdescribes it (§E.3)
Policy Binding Entitlement scope · counterparty concentration limits · permitted-instrument list by mandate · regulatory posture resolved at the decision instant from the ledger. Every bundle version in force lands in ProductLineage.policy_bundle_versions
Lineage ProductLineage exactly, and nothing more — operators_invoked (typed operator references), policy_bundle_versions, graph_snapshot_at. See §B.7 for where the rest of the governance evidence lives, and why it is not duplicated here
Semantic Version v1.0.0
Discovery treasury.liquidity-position.v1
Addressability /context-products/treasury/liquidity-position/{lei}
Assembly Mode 1 — no model in the trust path. Every figure is arithmetic over typed inputs. Chosen for determinism: a product whose whole claim is how old is each number cannot have a generative stage that could smooth two ages into one sentence

Mode 1 follows from the nature of the promise: deterministic arithmetic must retain the separate ages and policy bases of its inputs. The payload is classified internal, the highest input classification. Jurisdiction admission occurs before composition. An excluded deposit leaves no count, placeholder or “accounts hidden” marker; totals are computed over admitted evidence.

Parameter Type Moves Default
lei string(20), required E anchor —
intent enum operating-liquidity | reserve-buffer | short-term-investment, required P — selects the limit regime and the posture row —
as_of datetime, required T — the decision instant —
freshness string, required T — the currency the caller requires —
max_staleness mapping signal class → duration, or a single duration naming one class T — tightens a NAMED class's bound; never all of them (§B.6) the class profile
currencies list R scope — and therefore which FX observations participate at all all held
debt_tolerance float P — debt gate class default
horizon enum intraday | t+1 | t+30 T window intraday
include_proposals bool — inert — refuses not_supported_at_tier

The four request axes belong on first-class ProductRequest fields: subject, intent, asked_at and freshness. Only the class-specific remainder goes into parameters. This is how the architect preserves the identity of the question for addressing and replay.

max_staleness tightens a named class. It is not a universal age limit. currencies determines which FX observations participate, so removing an unused currency must also remove its FX freshness obligation. include_proposals explicitly refuses not_supported_at_tier.

Signal class Bound Mandatory? Breach behavior
Intraday rate observation 15 min yes fail closed — refuse, naming the signal and its age
FX reference observation 1 day yes when a conversion is required fail closed for the currencies that need it
Filing-period cash 90 days no serves, with a debt contribution and the period end shown
Concentration limit 90 days no serves; the verdict stands with its age published
Permitted-instrument list 90 days no serves; mandate check reported NOT_EVALUABLE if absent
Regulatory posture n/a — effectivity, not age yes a posture is never stale; it is in force or it is not (§D.3)
Deposit balance, investment position none — unobserved — no staleness claim is possible and none is made

The profile is a contract the SME can review: intraday rates have a 15-minute bound, FX one day, while policy follows effectivity and undated holdings have no claimable observation age. The three-field ProductLineage remains operators_invoked, policy_bundle_versions, graph_snapshot_at. Other governance evidence belongs on the surfaces assigned in §B.7 rather than being copied into lineage.

Let source measurements challenge the first design — Standard §C → final §C

The architect discovers that heldAt and concentratedIn describe the same measured deposit-edge population. Composing both would double count. Concentration uses the declared predicate and preserves one exposure per relationship.

Deposit and investment holdings have no observation timestamps. Their age is unobserved; assigning the request instant would manufacture freshness. A cash filing's period end is a reporting boundary, not a market observation time. These findings create four temporal classes in final §D.3:

Class What the date means Consequence for the answer
Market observation The signal was observed then Select at or before the decision instant and assess its declared cadence.
Policy effectivity The rule became applicable then Resolve the in-force rule; elapsed age alone does not make it stale.
Reporting period end The reported quantity concerns that period Preserve the period and knowability boundary; do not relabel it a market quote.
Unobserved holding No observation date is supplied Publish the limitation; make no freshness assertion for it.

The mandate check needs a meaningful negative control. All 15 measured mandates permit the three instrument kinds, making a kind-only test vacuous. The maximum tenor of 365 days does bite: 34 of 200 estate instruments, including two of the anchor's 14, exceed it. The spec uses that measured distinction instead of inventing an instrument prohibition.

Choose scenarios from real source windows — Standard §D → final §D

The source feeds occupy different time windows. The SME and architect choose three measured instants rather than fabricate timestamps to make every series look contemporaneous.

At 17 June 2026, 18:05Z, the intraday two-year rate is 4.285995%, against 4.05% in the 16 June daily observation: a 23.60 bp difference. For the relevant US-NY reserve-buffer case, enhanced scrutiny became effective on 16 June. The 15 June scenario therefore resolves a different posture and policy version. The rate's observation clock and the policy's effectivity clock both matter, for different reasons.

At 21 August, 16:00Z, the stale-signal scenario refuses service. The oldest participating intraday signal is 45 minutes old against a 15-minute bound. A USD-only request removes unnecessary FX participation, but cannot repair a stale mandatory liquidity signal. The final response contains no liquidity figure in this case.

The recipe resolves request identity, admits scope, acquires typed evidence, applies the four temporal rules, evaluates limits and mandate eligibility, and constructs the result. Replay pins the decision instant and source evidence. Neither the current wall clock nor a convenient latest value can silently move the question.

Explain debt and readiness in business terms — Standard §E–§F → final §E–§F

The declared debt basis is 1 − F×C×S. Freshness uses participating freshness-bearing classes; policy effectivity and undated holdings do not become fabricated timestamp observations. Completeness includes identity resolution and limit coverage, and semantic coherence includes currencies. Missing concentration limits raise debt and create an unevaluable verdict rather than an invented limit.

The example records additional declared debt treatments: 0.1 per missing-limit pair capped at 0.2, 0.08 for missing cash and 0.05 for missing mandate, with a default tolerance of 0.25. These are specification values. A mandatory intraday signal or policy failure is a refusal, not merely another optional penalty. Missing optional evidence and stale mandatory participating evidence must remain distinct cases.

Production is on demand. The identity/cache scope includes the declared temporal, currency, intent, principal and tolerance choices. TTL is 15 minutes from decision as a technical ceiling; a request pinned to a past instant is disclosed as a non-decaying forensic reconstruction. The final TBC register is closed, which is a documented readiness state rather than a new runtime certification by this companion.

Show what must fail when the design is broken — Standard §G → final §G

id asserts detects
TLP-G01 a plan with zero operator steps never serves empty-operator
TLP-G02 served lineage equals the plan's typed operator references exactly lineage drift
TLP-G03 expires_at derives from the decision instant and never exceeds the 15-minute ceiling TTL fabrication
TLP-G04 D_c above debt_tolerance returns 409 with the debt block ungated debt
TLP-G05 a withheld element leaves no count, marker or placeholder disclosure by marker
TLP-G06 payload classification is the highest of any contributing element classification leak
TLP-G07 at 2026-08-21T16:00Z with 15m, the product refuses and names SIG-000 at 45.0 min staleness gate inert
TLP-G08 that refusal carries no liquidity figure partial serve dressed as a warning
TLP-G09 2026-06-15T18:05Z and 2026-06-17T18:05Z return standard / enhanced-scrutiny and different policy_version as_of not reaching the policy leg
TLP-G10 a pre-flip request does not see the 2026-06-16 version though it is the ledger head reading head instead of effectivity
TLP-G11 the served 2-year rate at 2026-06-17T18:05Z is the tick (4.285995), not the published daily close (4.05), differing by ≥ 8 bp Latency Poisoned
TLP-G12 the anchor returns exactly 1 breach, 3 within-limit, 3 limit-unknown collapsing three verdicts into two
TLP-G13 the payload publishes limit coverage as a ratio (4/7) unstated completeness
TLP-G14 every payload element carries a temporal_class, and reported_cash is never market-observation flattening four clocks into one
TLP-G15 holdings carry no observed_at and none is synthesized from asked_at manufactured freshness
TLP-G16 at 2026-06-17T18:05Z the anchor reports 2 positions exceeding the 365-day mandate tenor (POS-00025 at 378 d, POS-00028 at 368 d) inert mandate check
TLP-G17 an LEI with no treasury_client row returns 404, distinct from a client with no positions request-error vs world-fact confusion
TLP-G18 the product reads one of heldAt / concentratedIn and records which claiming information the estate does not carry
TLP-G19 subject, intent, asked_at and freshness are ProductRequest FIELDS, and none of them also appears in parameters request identity demoted to a parameter, and hashed twice
TLP-G20 with currencies=["USD"] on a USD-home client, no FX observation participates and no FX bound can fire freshness deciding admission before scope decides participation
TLP-G21 the payload carries no second copy of D_c, the content address or the policy-bundle versions two copies of one figure, free to disagree
TLP-G22 at 2026-08-21T16:00Z the participating signal set is exactly the four LIQ-*-INTRADAY rows, and SIG-000 is the named refusal a stale-fixture demonstration preempted by an older signal nobody scoped out

The ten closing acceptance criteria require the three scenarios, the three concentration verdicts, all four temporal classes, exact replay, scoped freshness, increased debt when a limit is removed, first-class request axes and the exact lineage shape. The 22 gates must execute and include deliberate failures. The SME can then verify that “usable liquidity” never conceals absent limits or incomparable clocks, and the architect has the precise contract that produces that answer.

Current operations: use the refreshed implementation walkthrough and Fluree 4.2.4 where required. Embedded specifications remain historical evidence at their stated pins.

# Treasury Liquidity Position — Context Product Specification

**`CP-SPEC-009` · Tier 3 · `treasury.liquidity-position.v1`**
**PostgreSQL for balances, positions, rates and limits · Fluree for the position graph and the time-versioned regulatory posture**

> **What is this client's cash and rate posture at this instant, what may they
> do with it, and how old is each thing I just told you?**
>
> One question, over four kinds of time.

## 0 · What this document is

A build specification for the engineer who will assemble this Context Product
from the treasury data estate. It states the decision the product serves, the
contract it publishes, which store each element comes from, the assembly
recipe, and the gates the finished product is held to.

Every figure below was measured against the live estate on 2026-09-11 before
this document was written, and the query that produced it is reproducible.

### 0.1 The governing principle

Ruled by Dave at Gate 1, and it is the spine of every section that follows:

> **Different context elements have different temporal semantics. `as_of`
> governs the determination, but it does not turn reporting-period dates,
> market observations, policy effectivity and timeless holdings into the same
> kind of timestamp.**

Rungs 1 through 8 each carried one clock, or two of the same kind. This rung
carries **four kinds at once**, and the product's job is to keep them apart in
the payload rather than averaging them into a single freshness claim. §D.3 is
where that becomes mechanism.

### 0.2 Placeholder discipline

No `[TBC]`. Where a value is a demonstration choice rather than a production
recommendation, §0.4 names it and says why.

### 0.3 Reads only — no write path anywhere in this product

Both source stores are read. The ledger is append-only, so a write is
permanent; nothing in this product's assembly, its examples or its tests writes
to either store. The fabric's own graph is per-run scratch and is discarded
when the run exits.

This matters to the recipe and not only to operations: §D.6's replay
demonstration and §D.4's three scenarios are all reachable by moving one
request parameter, so no scenario needs the estate mutated to produce it.

### 0.4 What is real in this estate, and what was engineered

| Element | Provenance |
|---|---|
| Daily Treasury constant-maturity and SOFR series | **public** — FRED (`DGS3MO`…`DGS30`, `SOFR`, percentiles) |
| Daily par yield curve | **public** — Treasury.gov |
| FX daily reference rates | **public** — FRED (`DEXUSEU` and siblings) |
| **Intraday rate tick series** | **synthetic, deliberately engineered** — see below |
| **Intraday FX tick series** | **synthetic, deliberately engineered** |
| **`stale_signal` fixture** | **synthetic, deliberately engineered** — the `max_staleness` case |
| Client reported cash and its period end | **public** — XBRL `companyfacts` balance-sheet anchor |
| Deposit balances, investment positions | **synthetic** — internal treasury records have no public equivalent |
| Concentration limits, permitted-instrument lists, mandates | **synthetic** — internal treasury policy |
| Regulatory posture overlay and its versions | **synthetic** — internal, time-versioned in the ledger |

**The intraday tick series is the one engineered element this product depends
on, and it is engineered because it cannot be sourced.** Treasury.gov, FRED and
the NY Fed all publish **daily**. This product's entire premise is a signal that
moves within the day. Presenting interpolated ticks as observed market data
would misrepresent the source, so every tick row carries
`provenance = 'synthetic — engineered'` and the payload repeats it.

**Measured:** 11,700 tick rows · 30 trading days 2026-05-11 → 2026-06-23 ·
5 tenors (0.25, 1, 2, 5, 10 years) · 5-minute granularity · 13:30–19:55 UTC
(09:30–15:55 ET) · 78 ticks per tenor per day · 150 distinct (day, tenor) pairs.
The vault's manufacture envelope asked for at least one day carrying an 8 bp
intraday move; the largest measured is **24.33 bp** (2-year, 2026-05-26).

**Illustrative calibration.** This example runs against a point-in-time
demonstration estate rather than continuously refreshed production data.
Freshness half-lives and related thresholds are calibrated to make the governed
behavior observable in that snapshot. They demonstrate how the SDK applies
these controls and should not be interpreted as recommended production
coverage-policy thresholds. §E.1 carries the table; §D.4 carries the decision
instants and how each was chosen.

### 0.5 The four-question test

- **Is the answer assembled rather than stored?** Yes. No store holds *"this
  client's liquidity posture at 18:05 on 2026-06-17, under the regulatory
  posture then in force."* It is a rate observation from one table, holdings
  from two more, limits from a fourth, a currency conversion from a fifth, and
  a policy version reconstructed from a ledger — with four different temporal
  semantics that must survive into the payload.
- **Does more than one consumer need it?** Yes — the treasury specialist
  advising the client, the credit officer who owns the concentration limits,
  and the control function that has to show which policy version authorized a
  position. They want the same numbers with different envelopes.
- **Does it carry a governed freshness claim?** Yes, and an asymmetric one:
  15 minutes on the rate leg, 90 days on the filing leg, a step function on the
  policy leg, and — measured — **nothing at all on the holdings leg**, because
  the estate never recorded when a balance was observed. Publishing that
  absence is part of the claim.
- **Would a `SELECT` do?** No. A `SELECT` joining balances to the most recent
  published daily curve returns a confident number that is **23.60 bp** away
  from the market at the decision instant (§A.2), reports the client compliant
  when three of its seven counterparty exposures have no limit to check against
  (§A.3), and attaches one freshness to all of it.

---

## A · Decision frame

**The decision.** A treasury specialist advising a corporate client on cash
positioning or short-duration investment — intraday, while the client waits.

**The trigger.** The client asks a question whose answer moves within the hour.

**Consuming principals.** A single role at this tier. The conversational
advisory rendering is deferred to Tier 5.

### A.1 Counterfactuals — two, and they live at two instants

The vault names two failure modes. Measurement shows they **cannot both be
demonstrated in one run**, because the estate engineered them at different
decision instants. That is a property of the data, recorded here rather than
papered over, and it is why §D.4 defines three scenarios.

**`temporally-incoherent` — Latency Poisoned.** The rate-curve refresh is
daily. The frame is *correct against its pipeline contract* and *wrong against
the decision at hand*. Nothing is broken; the pipeline delivered exactly what
it promised, and the promise was the wrong one. Every system reports healthy.

**`policy-blind` — the limit that was never checked.** The agent reports a
client's concentration as compliant. Access control said yes. But three of the
client's seven counterparty exposures have **no concentration limit on file**,
and one of those three is larger than two of the limits that do exist. The
naive answer and the governed answer differ not in the numbers they compute but
in **what they admit they could not check**.

### A.2 The worked case — Latency Poisoned, measured

Anchor: `2549004GGE2APGNT6O92` (American Healthcare REIT, Inc.), the one
treasury client holding US-NY deposits under a `reserve-buffer` mandate.

Decision instant: **2026-06-17T18:05:00Z** (14:05 ET).

| | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| 2-year rate the product serves | **4.285995 %** | `intraday_tick`, `obs_ts = 2026-06-17T18:05Z` |
| 2-year rate the daily pipeline serves | **4.05 %** | `reference_rate`, `DGS2`, most recent *published* `obs_date = 2026-06-16` |
| **gap** | **23.60 bp** | measured |

The acceptance test, as a procedure that can fail:

1. Serve the product at `as_of = 2026-06-17T18:05:00Z`.
2. Read the 2-year rate the payload carries and its `observed_at`.
3. Independently read the most recent `reference_rate` row for `DGS2` with
   `obs_date < 2026-06-17`.
4. **Assert the two differ by at least 8 bp, and assert the served value is the
   tick.** If they agree, the product is reading the daily series and the
   intraday leg is decorative.

This is `TLP-G11`.

### A.3 The worked case — Policy Blind, measured

Same anchor, same instant. Fourteen positions, 2,630,266,766.99 in notional
across **seven** counterparties, against **four** concentration limits.

| counterparty | share of notional | limit | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `JJAX4X60DE65EYFOTY73` | 30.21 % | 30.2 % | **breach** |
| `549300EZQXWQI2YL1T80` | 17.08 % | — | **limit-unknown** |
| `0IDE18EMH1CUKQCUYE69` | 16.73 % | 18.7 % | within-limit |
| `529900E95812SYWMCE44` | 12.55 % | — | **limit-unknown** |
| `549300DUOO1KXOHPM605` | 11.87 % | 15.7 % | within-limit |
| `549300EC266625K12S42` | 11.52 % | 24 % | within-limit |
| `5493004PFHUPOR1PWN79` | 0.03 % | — | **limit-unknown** |

**The second-largest exposure this client holds has no limit to check it
against, and it is larger than two of the limits that exist.** A product with
two verdicts — breach and within-limit — reports six of seven as fine. A
product with three verdicts reports one breach, three within limit, and **three
it could not evaluate**, and publishes the coverage figure: **4 of 7
counterparties** here, **60 of 103 (holder, counterparty) pairs** estate-wide.

The acceptance test:

1. Serve the product for the anchor.
2. **Assert the payload distinguishes three verdicts, and that the count in
   each is 1 / 3 / 3.**
3. **Assert the payload publishes limit coverage as a ratio.**
4. Sabotage: collapse `limit-unknown` into `within-limit` and confirm the gate
   turns red.

This is `TLP-G12` and `TLP-G13`. No allocation optimizer is built — ruled at
Gate 1 (Q2 a). The demonstration uses the client's **real holdings**, so no
business logic is invented in example code.

### A.4 Scope boundary

**Held at §B.8**, where the Standard places it, together with the check against
§C and the payload that the scope-boundary field exists to receive.

---

## B · Contract

### B.1 The nine elements

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| **Schema** | `treasury_liquidity_position` — entities `cmns-org:LegalEntity`, `fibo-fbc-pas-caa:DepositAccount`, `fibo-fbc-pas-caa:InvestmentAccount`, `fibo-sec-dbt-bnd:TreasuryBill`, `fibo-sec-fun-fun:MutualFund`, `fibo-sec-dbt-tsd:CommercialPaper`; measures `fibo-ind-ir-ir:ReferenceInterestRate`, `fibo-ind-fx-fx:QuotedExchangeRate`, `fibo-fnd-acc-cur:MonetaryAmount`; relationships `ex:heldAt`, `ex:concentratedIn`, `ex:setOffAgainst`; policy `ex:RegulatoryPosture`. Machine-readable at `schemas/treasury_liquidity_position.v1.json` |
| **Freshness SLA** | **Per signal class, and the classes do not share a clock** — §B.6. Intraday rate 15 min · FX reference 1 day · filing-period cash 90 days · regulatory posture governed by effectivity, not by age · holdings **unobserved and therefore unclaimable** |
| **TTL** | 15 minutes · `ttl_anchor: from_decision`. `expires_at = decision_instant + 15m`. A request pinned to a past `as_of` is a forensic reconstruction and **does not decay**; the payload says so rather than publishing a window that misdescribes it (§E.3) |
| **Policy Binding** | Entitlement scope · counterparty concentration limits · permitted-instrument list by mandate · **regulatory posture resolved at the decision instant from the ledger**. Every bundle version in force lands in `ProductLineage.policy_bundle_versions` |
| **Lineage** | **`ProductLineage` exactly, and nothing more** — `operators_invoked` (typed operator references), `policy_bundle_versions`, `graph_snapshot_at`. See §B.7 for where the rest of the governance evidence lives, and why it is not duplicated here |
| **Semantic Version** | `v1.0.0` |
| **Discovery** | `treasury.liquidity-position.v1` |
| **Addressability** | `/context-products/treasury/liquidity-position/{lei}` |
| **Assembly Mode** | **1 — no model in the trust path.** Every figure is arithmetic over typed inputs. Chosen for determinism: a product whose whole claim is *how old is each number* cannot have a generative stage that could smooth two ages into one sentence |

`extra=forbid` on every payload model, validated at the boundary.

### B.2 Classification, residency and cross-border serving

**Data classification: `internal`** — the highest of any §C element. Deposit
balances, investment positions, concentration limits, permitted-instrument
lists and the regulatory-posture overlay are all internal; the rate, FX and
filing elements are public, and the highest governs the payload.

**Information barrier.** None crosses this product. It reads no MNPI-bearing
source and constructs no research or advisory content; a client's own treasury
position is visible to the coverage relationship that owns it.

**Residency.** Deposit accounts carry a jurisdiction (measured: `US-DE`, `GB`,
`US-NY`, `US-MD`, `DE`, `FR`, `IN`, `CN`) and the regulatory posture is keyed on
it. The product is served **from the tenant's own region**; no element is
replicated across a border by this product.

**Cross-border serving.** A principal whose `principal_jurisdiction` prefixes do
not cover a deposit's jurisdiction does not receive that deposit. The exclusion
is formative, not a filter applied afterward.

**The suppression rule.** Where policy excludes content the payload carries
**no count, no marker and no placeholder** — an excluded deposit is absent, and
the liquidity totals are computed over what remains. A *"2 accounts hidden"*
marker is itself a disclosure and is a gate failure (`TLP-G05`).

### B.3 Model-risk annotation

**Not applicable — no model in the trust path.** Assembly Mode 1. No LLM is
invoked at any stage; there is no prompt artifact, no temperature to pin and no
smoothing control to specify, because nothing in the path could reconcile a
conflict the substrate surfaced.

### B.4 Request parameter surface

| Parameter | Type | Moves | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lei` | string(20), required | `E` anchor | — |
| `intent` | enum `operating-liquidity` \| `reserve-buffer` \| `short-term-investment`, required | `P` — selects the limit regime and the posture row | — |
| `as_of` | datetime, required | **`T` — the decision instant** | — |
| `freshness` | string, required | `T` — the currency the caller requires | — |
| `max_staleness` | mapping `signal class → duration`, or a single duration naming one class | **`T` — tightens a NAMED class's bound; never all of them** (§B.6) | the class profile |
| `currencies` | list | `R` scope — **and therefore which FX observations participate at all** | all held |
| `debt_tolerance` | float | `P` — debt gate | class default |
| `horizon` | enum `intraday` \| `t+1` \| `t+30` | `T` window | `intraday` |
| `include_proposals` | bool | — | **inert — refuses `not_supported_at_tier`** |

### B.5 How the request maps onto the SDK — the four axes are identity, not parameters

**`ProductRequest` carries whitepaper §6.3's four axes as FIRST-CLASS fields.**
They establish *which question was asked*, they are what the content address
and the replay record resolve against, and putting any of them in `parameters`
would demote request identity to class-declared remainder. The mapping is
therefore fixed, and `TLP-G19` holds the product to it:

| The caller supplies | Lands on | Why it is not a parameter |
|---|---|---|
| the `{lei}` path segment | **`ProductRequest.subject`** | the entity anchor — *which entity* |
| `intent` | **`ProductRequest.intent`** | the decision being served — *for what decision* |
| `as_of` | **`ProductRequest.asked_at`** | the instant asked **as of** — *against what clock*. Supplied by the caller; the SDK never reads one (`D-IMPL-98`, `C-15`) |
| the freshness requirement | **`ProductRequest.freshness`** | *under what temporal claim* |
| `max_staleness`, `currencies`, `horizon`, `debt_tolerance`, `include_proposals` | **`ProductRequest.parameters`** | the class-declared remainder of the question |
| the product class and lane | `schema_name` = `treasury.liquidity-position.v1`, `schema_version` = `1.0.0` | — |

**`as_of` is `asked_at`, and the spelling matters.** This product has one
decision instant and it is the caller's, not the host's. A design that carried
`as_of` in `parameters` while `asked_at` defaulted to a clock would produce two
instants that agree until they do not, and replay would resolve against the
wrong one.

### B.6 The staleness profile — the refusal rule is per class, not one clock

**The `max_staleness` bound is declared per signal class in the Control Plane,
and a request tightens a NAMED class.** Flattening the classes into one
15-minute clock would refuse the product on its filing evidence — which is a
quarterly figure and is *supposed* to be months old — and would make the 15
minutes meaningless by applying it to something that never moves that fast.

| Signal class | Bound | Mandatory? | Breach behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intraday rate observation | **15 min** | **yes** | **fail closed** — refuse, naming the signal and its age |
| FX reference observation | **1 day** | yes *when a conversion is required* | **fail closed** for the currencies that need it |
| Filing-period cash | **90 days** | no | serves, with a debt contribution and the period end shown |
| Concentration limit | 90 days | no | serves; the verdict stands with its age published |
| Permitted-instrument list | 90 days | no | serves; mandate check reported `NOT_EVALUABLE` if absent |
| Regulatory posture | **n/a — effectivity, not age** | **yes** | a posture is never stale; it is in force or it is not (§D.3) |
| Deposit balance, investment position | **none — unobserved** | — | **no staleness claim is possible and none is made** |

Three consequences, each gated:

- **A class participates only if the request needs it.** `currencies=["USD"]`
  for a USD-home client requires no conversion, so **no FX observation
  participates** and no FX bound can fire. Scope decides participation before
  freshness decides admission (`TLP-G20`).
- **The refusal names the class, the signal, its observed age and the bound it
  broke** — never a bare "stale".
- **A non-mandatory class never refuses.** It contributes debt (§E.2). The
  15-minute figure governs one row of this table and the product never lets it
  govern another.

### B.7 Where the governance evidence lives — and why lineage does not carry it

**`ProductLineage` is three fields.** `operators_invoked`,
`policy_bundle_versions`, `graph_snapshot_at`. It is the L axis as it appears on
a delivered product, and this specification does **not** extend it.

Everything else this product must evidence has a surface of its own, and
duplicating it into the payload or the lineage would create two copies that can
disagree:

| Evidence | Where it lives | Not in lineage because |
|---|---|---|
| Per-signal `observed_at` and `temporal_class` | the **payload's signal register** — it is the product's answer, not its provenance | a consumer reads it to act, not to audit |
| `D_c` and its components | the **DebtAssessment** surface | debt is a measured property of the serve, resolved with the effective tolerance and its authority |
| The content address | the **governed product**'s address | it is a hash over the whole answer including the lineage |
| Model record, prompt artifact | **nothing — Assembly Mode 1** | there is no model in the path |
| Projection plan, perspective | the **replay record's** dimension 4 | replay resolves it; the payload does not restate it |
| The instant asked as-of | `ProductRequest.asked_at`, carried into replay | it is request identity (§B.5) |

`TLP-G02` asserts lineage strict equality over exactly the three fields, and
`TLP-G21` asserts the payload does **not** carry a second copy of the debt
figure, the content address or the policy versions.

### B.8 Prerequisites, consumers and scope boundary

**Prerequisites** (vault): `counterparty-reference-snapshot` (rung 1) for
counterparty identity; `collateral-and-setoff-coverage` (rung 6) for the deposit
population and its set-off flags.

**Consumers, named individually** — a reverse dependency list is what
supersession cascades and MAJOR-version notification need, and *"any treasury
consumer"* cannot serve as one:

| Consumer | What it takes | Notified on |
|---|---|---|
| `credit-surveillance-early-warning` (rung 11) | the concentration verdicts and their coverage ratio | MAJOR; and on any posture supersession (§E.4) |
| `fx-post-trade-reconciliation` (rung 12) | the FX observation set and its instants | MAJOR |
| `large-exposure-rwa-concentration` (rung 21) | counterparty concentration as one input to the group denominator | MAJOR |

No rung below 9 consumes this product.

**Scope boundary — the vault's sentence, verbatim:** *a corporate client's cash,
rate, and concentration posture right now.*

Checked against §C and the payload, three boundaries are drawn explicitly:

- **No allocation proposals.** `include_proposals` is declared and **refuses
  with `not_supported_at_tier`** rather than silently returning nothing.
  Generating candidate allocations requires an optimization policy that is
  domain configuration, not SDK mechanism.
- **No FX exposure product.** Currency conversion happens so liquidity can be
  expressed in one currency; the FX *position* question is rung 12's.
- **No collateral or set-off computation.** `deposit_account` carries
  `setoff_contractual` and `setoff_enforceable`, and 73 of 120 deposits carry a
  `nettedUnder` edge. That is rung 6's subject. This product reads the flags
  through and does not net.

**No conflict found.** The payload declares no field the vault's scope excludes.

### C.1 Element table

**The IRI column is the vault's Wave-8 binding mirror, not this document's
proposal.** `fibo-iri-binding` names the deposit/investment classes under
*DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS (collateral-and-setoff, treasury-liquidity)* and the rate and
FX classes under *RATES / FX REFERENCE (treasury-liquidity, fx-post-trade)*. Two
bindings in this table's first draft were wrong against it and were corrected
rather than argued: reported cash is `fibo-fnd-acc-cur:MonetaryAmount` (there is
no bound `CashInstrument`), and the FX rate is `fibo-ind-fx-fx:QuotedExchangeRate`
(not `fibo-fbc-fi-fi:ExchangeRate`). The `ex:` terms — `ConcentrationLimit`,
`PermittedInstrument`, `RegulatoryPosture`, `heldAt`, `concentratedIn`,
`setOffAgainst` — are deliberately unbound: no FIBO or Commons term covers them,
and inventing a `spec.edmcouncil.org` IRI for an internal concept would make the
binding mirror disagree with FIBO.

Deployment detail — host, port, credential — appears nowhere in this
specification, in the example tree, or in any artifact. `backends.yaml` carries
environment-variable **names** only.

### C.2 The population, measured 2026-09-11

| | measured |
|---|---|
| Treasury clients | **15**, all resolving in `ccf_v2.legal_entity` |
| Intents | 5 each of `operating-liquidity`, `reserve-buffer`, `short-term-investment` |
| Deposit accounts | **120** · 4 currencies (JPY 32, GBP 30, EUR 29, USD 29) · 8 jurisdictions · 7–9 per client |
| Investment positions | **200** · 3 kinds (T-bill 70, MMF 68, CP 62) · 13–14 per client · 45 counterparties, **45 of 45 resolving** |
| Concentration limits | **60** · exactly 4 per client · every limit row matches a real position pair · **60 of 103 position pairs covered** |
| Permitted-instrument rows | **45** — all 15 mandates permit all 3 kinds at **365 days** |
| Intraday ticks | **11,700** · 30 days · 5 tenors · 5-minute |
| Daily reference rates | **10,539** · 16 series · 659 dates · 2024-01-02 → 2026-08-20 |
| FX daily | **3,942** · 6 pairs → 2026-08-14 · FX intraday **10,368** · 2026-08-06 → 08-13 only |
| `stale_signal` | **4** rows, own `as_of` 2026-08-21T16:00Z · ages 45.0 / 2.5 / 1.28 / 1.55 min |
| Regulatory postures | **13** nodes over **12** occurring (jurisdiction, intent) pairs |
| **Posture versions** | **exactly one pair is versioned** — `US-NY / reserve-buffer`: `standard` from 2024-01-02, `enhanced-scrutiny` from **2026-06-16** |
| Concentration breaches on real holdings | **10 pairs across 9 clients** |
| Mandate tenor exceedances at 2026-06-17 | **34 of 200 positions** |

### C.3 Correlation key, single-writer, identity authority

**Key.** `LEI` end to end. Client → `treasury_client.lei` → `deposit_account.holder_lei`
→ `investment_position.holder_lei` → `investment_position.counterparty_lei` →
`legal_entity.lei`. In the ledger, counterparty nodes carry `ex:lei`, so the
graph and relational legs join on the same authority with no crosswalk.
**Measured coverage: 15 of 15 clients and 45 of 45 counterparties resolve.**

**Identity authority.** GLEIF for counterparty identity; the internal treasury
register for client registration and mandate. These are different authorities
with different freshness ceilings and the payload does not average them.

**Single writer.** Nothing here writes. Both legs are read through L2 into the
per-run fabric graph; the ArtifactStore holds the served product and its replay
record. No harness and no operator acquires a write handle.

### C.4 The data traps

Six, each with the binding chosen and what the choice costs.

- **`heldAt` and `concentratedIn` are the same edge, twice.** Both exist on all
  200 `InvestmentAccount` nodes, and **0 of 200 diverge**. The vault's design
  treats them as two relationship types; the estate materializes one relation
  under two names. **Binding:** read `ex:concentratedIn` for the concentration
  question, record which predicate answered, and do **not** compose the two as
  if they carried different information. **Cost:** the traversal is one hop, not
  two, and the product says so (`TLP-G18`).
- **Holdings carry no observation time.** `deposit_account` and
  `investment_position` have no timestamp column at all. **Binding:** a fourth
  temporal class, `unobserved-holding`, with no `observed_at` and no
  contribution to the freshness term. **Cost:** the product cannot make a
  freshness claim about the client's own balances, and it publishes that
  absence rather than inheriting the request time (`TLP-G15`). This is the
  sharpest finding in the estate and it contradicts the vault's "deposit
  balances ~1 hour" row, which assumed a timestamp that is not there.
- **`cash_fact_asof` is a reporting-period end, not an observation instant.**
  Measured values are 2022-12-31, 2025-09-30, 2026-03-31 (×3), 2026-06-27,
  2026-06-30 (×9) — quarter ends from XBRL `companyfacts`. **Binding:**
  `temporal_class: reporting-period-end`, its own slow λ_c, never decayed as a
  market observation. **Cost:** one client's reported cash is 3.5 years old, and
  the payload shows that beside a 15-minute rate — which is the asymmetry the
  rung exists to make visible.
- **The permitted-instrument *kind* check is vacuous; the *tenor* check is
  not.** All 15 mandates permit all 3 instrument kinds, so no position is ever
  refused on kind. The 365-day maximum tenor does bite: **34 of 200** positions
  exceed it at 2026-06-17, including 2 of the anchor's 14. **Binding:** run both
  checks and report them separately, so a reader can see which one discriminated.
  **Cost:** honesty about a control that never fires in this estate.
- **The intraday series, the FX intraday series, the daily series, the stale
  fixture and the filing dates occupy five different time universes.** Latest
  tick 2026-06-23; FX intraday 2026-08-06→08-13; FX daily → 2026-08-14; daily
  rates → 2026-08-20; the stale fixture pinned at 2026-08-21. **Binding:** three
  pinned scenarios (§D.4), each chosen from a measurement. **Cost:** there is no
  single instant at which the whole product is live, and pretending otherwise
  would make every answer `fail_closed` — the cp-07 failure, avoided by ruling
  rather than by luck.
- **Concentration limits cover 58 % of exposure pairs.** 60 of 103. **Binding:**
  a third verdict, `limit-unknown`, and a published coverage ratio. **Cost:**
  the product cannot say "compliant"; it says "1 breach, 3 within limit, 3 not
  evaluable, coverage 4/7."

## D · Assembly recipe

### D.1 Client call

The forensic case, because it exercises the most surface:

```
GET /context-products/treasury/liquidity-position/2549004GGE2APGNT6O92
      ?intent=reserve-buffer
      &as_of=2026-06-17T18:05:00Z
      &max_staleness=intraday-rate:15m
      &debt_tolerance=0.25
```

The same question as a `ProductRequest`, so the §B.5 mapping is concrete rather
than described. **Four axes are fields; the remainder is `parameters`:**

```
ProductRequest(
    schema_name="treasury.liquidity-position.v1",
    schema_version="1.0.0",
    subject="2549004GGE2APGNT6O92",            # the {lei} path segment
    intent="reserve-buffer",
    asked_at=datetime(2026, 6, 17, 18, 5, tzinfo=timezone.utc),   # `as_of`
    freshness="intraday",
    parameters={
        "max_staleness": {"intraday-rate": "PT15M"},
        "horizon": "intraday",
        "debt_tolerance": 0.25,
    },
)
```

Note what is **absent** from `parameters`: no `lei`, no `intent`, no `as_of`.
Each is already an axis, and a second copy in `parameters` would be a value the
content address hashes twice and replay could resolve two ways.

### D.2 Step table

| # | Operator | Capability | Inputs | Emits | Failure behavior | p95 budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Resolve` | relational | `lei`, `intent` | client registration, mandate, home currency, filing-period cash | `404` on unknown anchor | 301 ms † |
| 2 | `Policy` | bitemporal-ledger | client jurisdictions, `intent`, `as_of` | posture in force per (jurisdiction, intent) + `policy_version` | `503` if the ledger is unreachable | 301 ms † |
| 3 | `Traversal` | graph-traversal | client URI, `as_of` | position graph — `concentratedIn` to counterparties | `503` if the ledger is unreachable | 301 ms † |
| 4 | `Enrich` | relational | position graph, `as_of`, currency set | balances, notionals, the rate tick at `as_of`, the FX observation, **each with its own `observed_at` and `temporal_class`** | `503` naming the absent source class | 301 ms † |
| 5 | `Evaluate` | in-memory | everything above, `max_staleness` | **staleness gate**, then liquidity by currency and in home currency, weighted duration, concentration verdicts, mandate checks | **fail closed** naming the class, the signal, its age and the bound (§B.6) | 594 ms ‡ |
| 6 | `Projection` | in-memory | evaluated measures, posture | the principal's view | — | 594 ms ‡ |
| 7 | — | in-memory | all of the above | contract assembly, `payload_hash`, `D_c`, TTL | `409` on debt gate | 594 ms ‡ |

**THE BUDGETS ARE MEASURED, AND THE GRANULARITY IS STATED RATHER THAN
IMPLIED.** Seven runs against the live estate at `db559c65`, p95:

| phase | p50 | p95 | steps it covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| boot | 64 ms | 69 ms | registration and the fabric's own L3 |
| † acquire | 301 ms | 499 ms | steps 1–4 — both source reads |
| ingest | 628 ms | 764 ms | L1 → L2 → L3, the single-writer path |
| ‡ govern | 396 ms | 594 ms | steps 5–7 — gates, Π, debt, replay, delivery |
| **total** | **1,494 ms** | **1,703 ms** | |

**Per-operator instrumentation was not built**, so the budget is attributed at
phase granularity and the two marks say which steps share a figure. A
per-operator number would have to be invented to fill this table at step
granularity, and an invented budget that survives review becomes a number
somebody plans against.

**Against the envelope: 1.70 s of a 900-second TTL — 0.19 %.** The dominating
phase is **ingest**, not either source read, and that is a property of this
deployment rather than of the fabric: 41 nodes and 47 edges are written one
envelope at a time through the single write handle. The first optimization
would be batching that write path; it is not taken here, because the product's
subject is temporal semantics rather than throughput, and a batched ingest
would obscure the ordering contract §D.2's own prose depends on.

Operators come from the closed vocabulary. The staleness gate is **inside step
5**, not a step of its own — it is an `Evaluate` precondition, and making it a
step would put an operator in the plan that emits nothing.

**Policy runs before traversal and before enrichment.** At this tier the
posture does not remove edges, but it must be *resolved at the decision
instant* before any measure is computed, so that the answer and the authority
for the answer come from the same moment. Mirroring this into `artifacts/assembly-recipe.yaml`
with a WITNESS per step is a Gate 2 obligation.

### D.3 The four temporal classes — this rung's mechanism

Every element the payload carries declares a `temporal_class`. The classes are
not interchangeable and the product's arithmetic treats them differently.

| class | example | what the timestamp means | how `as_of` acts on it | decays? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `market-observation` | `intraday_tick.obs_ts`, `fx_reference_rate.obs_date` | an instant at which a value was observed | **selects** the observation at or before `as_of` | **yes** — against ITS OWN λ_c, and subject to ITS OWN §B.6 bound |
| `policy-effectivity` | `RegulatoryPosture.validFrom` | the instant from which a rule is in force | **selects** the version in force at `as_of` | **no** — a step function. A policy is not stale; it is either in force or it is not |
| `reporting-period-end` | `treasury_client.cash_fact_asof` | the closing label of a reporting window | **bounds** it — a period ending after `as_of` is not yet knowable | slowly, on filing cadence — never on market cadence |
| `unobserved-holding` | `deposit_account.balance`, `investment_position.notional` | **nothing — no observation time was recorded** | **does not act on it at all** | **undefined**, and the payload says so |

Three consequences that the gates enforce:

- A `reporting-period-end` never enters the freshness term (`TLP-G14`).
- An `unobserved-holding` never receives a synthesized `observed_at` from the
  request time (`TLP-G15`). Inheriting `asked_at` would manufacture a freshness
  claim out of the act of asking.
- `policy-effectivity` is resolved by comparing `validFrom` to `as_of`, not by
  reading the ledger head (`TLP-G10`).

### D.4 The three scenarios, and how each instant was chosen

Ruled at Gate 1 (Q1 a). Every instant below comes from a measurement, not a
preference.

**Scenario 1 — the headline run. `as_of = 2026-06-17T18:05:00Z`.**
Chosen because it is the **largest measured gap between the intraday tick and
the most recent published daily close, anywhere in the post-flip window**:
2-year tick 4.285995 % against `DGS2` 4.05 % published 2026-06-16 — **23.60 bp**.
The posture flip of 2026-06-16 is in force, so `US-NY / reserve-buffer` reads
`enhanced-scrutiny`. Carries the Latency-Poisoned counterfactual (`TLP-G11`),
the three concentration verdicts (`TLP-G12`), and 2 mandate tenor exceedances.

**Scenario 2 — policy time-travel. `as_of = 2026-06-15T18:05:00Z`.**
Same client, same question, same parameters, **two days earlier and one posture
version back.** `US-NY / reserve-buffer` reads `standard`, and `policy_version`
differs. Chosen as the last trading day before the flip. The assertion is that
the two runs **disagree** — if they agree, the effectivity filter was dropped
and `as_of` is not reaching the policy leg (`TLP-G09`).

**Scenario 3 — fail closed. `as_of = 2026-08-21T16:00:00Z`,
`max_staleness = {intraday-rate: 15m}`, `currencies = ["USD"]`.**

The `stale_signal` fixture's own instant, and **the scenario has to declare its
participating signal set or `SIG-000` is preempted by something older.** This is
a real property of the estate, measured, and it is stated here rather than
discovered during the build:

| feed | newest observation at 2026-08-21T16:00Z | age |
|---|---|---|
| `stale_signal` (`LIQ-*-INTRADAY`) | 2026-08-21 15:58:43Z | **1.28 – 45.0 min** |
| `intraday_tick` (the curve) | 2026-06-23 19:55Z | **59 days** |
| `fx_reference_rate` | 2026-08-14 | **7 days** |
| `reference_rate` (daily) | 2026-08-20 | 1 day |
| `cash_fact_asof` | 2026-06-30 | 52 days (period end, not an observation) |

Two scoping decisions make `SIG-000` the legitimately-named refusal:

- **The intraday-rate class is served from `stale_signal` at this instant, not
  from `intraday_tick`.** They are two engineered feeds for the same signal
  class covering **disjoint windows** — the curve feed for 2026-05-11 → 06-23,
  the `LIQ-*` feed for 2026-08-21. The product reads whichever source holds an
  observation at or before the decision instant; at 2026-08-21 `intraday_tick`
  holds none, so it is **absent from the answer rather than 59 days stale**, and
  a source with no observation in scope contributes no age. (A mandatory class
  with *no* source at all would be `503`, not a staleness refusal — §D.7. Here
  the class has a source.)
- **`currencies = ["USD"]` against a USD-home client means no conversion is
  required, so no FX observation participates** and the 7-day FX figure cannot
  fire (§B.6, `TLP-G20`). Scope decides participation before freshness decides
  admission. The anchor holds four USD deposit accounts totaling
  165,388,122.30, so this is a real question and not a narrowing invented to
  dodge the FX bound.

What remains participating is exactly the four `LIQ-*-INTRADAY` signals, of
which `SIG-000` at **45.0 minutes** is the only one over its 15-minute bound and
the oldest of the four. The product refuses, names `SIG-000`, its age and the
bound it broke, and **carries no liquidity figure at all** (`TLP-G07`,
`TLP-G08`, `TLP-G22`). A product that returned three-quarters of an answer with
a warning would pass a "did it warn?" test and fail this one.

### D.5 Determinism and the emitted contract

**Determinism class: `deterministic`.** No model in the trust path. Given the
same `as_of`, the same ledger `t` and the same Control Plane state, the product
returns byte-identical bytes. `payload_hash` is `sha256` over the canonical
bytes excluding `assembled_at`.

The envelope is the §8 response envelope, populated with types. **The payload
carries the answer; the governed surfaces carry the evidence** (§B.7), and the
split is deliberate — a figure duplicated across both is a figure that can
disagree with itself.

**Payload** — client identity and mandate; liquidity by currency and in home
currency with the FX observation used for each conversion; weighted duration
against the rate curve; per-counterparty concentration with its three-valued
verdict and the coverage ratio; the mandate kind and tenor checks reported
separately; the posture in force with its `validFrom` and version id;
filing-period cash with its period end; and **a signal register listing every
participating element with its `observed_at`, its `temporal_class` and its age
at the decision instant**.

**`ProductLineage`** — `operators_invoked`, `policy_bundle_versions`,
`graph_snapshot_at`. Three fields, and this product adds none. `TLP-G02` holds
the served set to strict equality against the plan's typed operator references.

**The other surfaces** — `D_c` and its components on the debt assessment,
resolved against the effective tolerance and the authority that established it;
the content address on the governed product; the operator plan, perspective and
request axes in the five-dimension replay record. `TLP-G21` asserts the payload
carries no second copy of any of them.

### D.6 Replay

1. Serve at `as_of = 2026-06-17T18:05:00Z`; record `payload_hash`,
   `graph_snapshot_at`, `policy_version`.
2. Re-serve at the same `as_of` without pinning the snapshot; confirm the hash
   is unchanged — the estate is static, so this proves reproducibility, not
   time-travel.
3. Re-serve at `as_of = 2026-06-15T18:05:00Z`; confirm the posture and
   `policy_version` **differ**, and that the hash differs.
4. Re-serve at `2026-06-17T18:05:00Z` again and confirm the **original** hash
   returns. If step 4 returns step 3's value, `as_of` is not reaching the plan
   and `graph_snapshot_at` is decorative.

Two axes, tested separately: the rate axis (`TLP-G11`) and the policy axis
(`TLP-G09`). **Agreement between them under a constructed case means a filter
was dropped.**

### D.7 Validation gates

Six universal, without re-argument: empty-operator guard · lineage strict
equality · TTL bounds · debt gate · suppression silence · classification
containment. These are `TLP-G01` … `TLP-G06`. The product-specific gates are
`TLP-G07` … `TLP-G22` and are tabulated in §G.1.

**Error mapping.**

| condition | raising step | response |
|---|---|---|
| `lei` has no `treasury_client` row | 1 | `404` — distinct from a client with no positions, which is `200` with an empty holdings block |
| principal not entitled to the client | 2 | `403`, no detail on what exists |
| `include_proposals=true` | 0 (validation) | `400 not_supported_at_tier` |
| a **participating, mandatory** signal class exceeds ITS bound (§B.6) | 5 | **refusal** naming the class, the signal, its age and the bound, **no partial payload**. A non-mandatory class never reaches here — it contributes debt |
| `D_c` exceeds `debt_tolerance` | 7 | `409` with the debt block |
| ledger or relational leg unreachable | 2, 3, 4 | `503` naming the source class |
| concentration limits absent for some counterparties | 5 | `200` with `limit-unknown` verdicts and the coverage ratio — **not** a silent pass |

**Silence is not a negative answer.** A counterparty with no limit row is not a
counterparty within its limit, and the payload never lets the two read the same.
